units: dx/dt and dy/dt in feet per second
models.objective: find dy/dt from x, y, L, and dx/dt at one instant
candidates: the supplied snapshot satisfying the fixed-length constraint
boundaries: x=L where the idealized ladder reaches the ground
models.interpretation: If the foot moves away from the wall, the top moves downward, so dy/dt is negative.
models.reasonableness: Check opposite rate signs, fixed-length geometry, and feet-per-second units.

units: dV/dt in cubic meters per minute
assumptions: tank and water are similar right circular cones
models.relation: r/h = R/H and V = pi r^2 h / 3
models.objective: express V using h alone and find dh/dt at the stated depth
models.derivative: after r=(R/H)h, differentiate V(h) with respect to time
models.interpretation: Positive inflow produces positive depth rate, with the rate depending on current cross-sectional area.
models.reasonableness: Check similarity, positive signs, and conversion from volume-per-time to length-per-time.

units: dx/dt and ds/dt in length per time
assumptions: one straight light ray defines the shadow tip
models.objective: find shadow-growth or shadow-tip rate from walking speed
models.derivative: differentiate the similar-triangle relation with respect to time
boundaries: large x where the ideal point-source model becomes less useful
models.interpretation: The shadow tip moves at dx/dt + ds/dt, not merely at the shadow-growth rate.
models.reasonableness: Check that the large triangle uses base x+s and that rate units match walking speed.

assumptions: the chosen angle matches the tangent relation
models.relation: tan(theta) = d/x for the angle shown
models.objective: find dtheta/dt from position and linear speed
models.feasibleDomain: x > 0 and d > 0 for the displayed acute angle
boundaries: closest approach x=0 requires a limiting or complementary-angle interpretation
models.interpretation: The sign states whether the sightline rotates toward or away from the reference direction.
models.reasonableness: Check radians-per-time units and the angle placement before selecting d/x or x/d.

units: x, y, P in length units
assumptions: area is the quantity to maximize
models.interpretation: The maximum occurs at x=y=P/4, so the best rectangle is a square.
models.reasonableness: Check dimensions, endpoint areas, symmetry, and square units.

variables: x: corner cut and box height
units: L, W, x in length units
assumptions: four equal corner squares are removed
remaining flaps fold without material thickness
models.derivative: differentiate the cubic V(x) and solve V'(x)=0
models.interpretation: The selected cut size becomes the box height and leaves positive base dimensions.
models.reasonableness: Reject roots outside the sheet geometry and compare every feasible candidate in cubic units.

assumptions: demand and cost functions are valid over the stated production range
quantity is modeled continuously for local analysis
models.feasibleDomain: q >= 0, demand price nonnegative, and capacity limits respected
candidates: quantities where marginal revenue equals marginal cost
models.interpretation: Profit rises where MR exceeds MC and falls where MC exceeds MR.
models.reasonableness: Check price, capacity, discrete rounding, endpoint profit, and dollar-per-unit interpretations.

units: C'(t) in concentration units per hour
assumptions: model is descriptive rather than individual medical advice
models.relation: C(t)=A t exp(-k t) for positive fitted parameters A and k
models.objective: identify rise, peak time, peak concentration, and decline
models.feasibleDomain: t >= 0 within the calibrated observation window
boundaries: end of the validated measurement range
models.interpretation: The peak occurs when C' changes from positive to negative.
models.reasonableness: Check nonnegative concentration, time units, observed calibration data, and patient-variation limitations.

units: a in distance per time squared
assumptions: road grade and traction are fixed
models.objective: measure stopping-distance sensitivity to a small speed increase
models.feasibleDomain: v >= 0 and a > 0 within measured road conditions
boundaries: maximum speed supported by the fitted conditions
models.interpretation: The derivative grows with speed because braking distance contributes a quadratic term.
models.reasonableness: Check distance units, increasing sensitivity, reaction and braking components, and wet-road or fatigue limitations.

units: x and dx in input units
f and dy in output units
f'(x) in output units per input unit
assumptions: f is differentiable near the nominal value
models.objective: estimate output tolerance from input tolerance
models.feasibleDomain: nominal input plus or minus tolerance remains inside the valid manufacturing domain
models.derivative: evaluate f'(x) at the nominal input
models.interpretation: The local slope is an uncertainty amplification factor.
models.reasonableness: Compare the differential estimate with endpoint evaluations when the tolerance is not tiny.

assumptions: the smooth cost curve approximates discrete production locally
q and q+1 remain in the feasible production range
models.objective: estimate the cost of producing one additional unit
candidates: the finite increment q to q+1
models.interpretation: Marginal cost is an instantaneous slope used as an approximation to a one-unit cost increase.
models.reasonableness: Check dollar-per-unit units and compare against the actual finite difference when available.
